title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp. 61-62): F is a set of 'figures' with a symmetric relation || ("apart", "disjoint"). There is a distinguished element ∅_F that is || to every figure, and it is the only figure that is || to itself. For A ⊂ F, cosupp A = {x ∈ F : x || a for all a ∈ A} is the polar (orthogonal) of A. Since || is symmetric, cosupp is an antitone Galois self-connection, and Ā = cosupp cosupp A is a closure operator. The closed parts are the 'F-supports'; they form Σ^0_F. Restricted to Σ^0_F, cosupp is an involutive antitone bijection, written ∁A. Grothendieck glosses it as 'the interior of the complementary support of A', the topological intuition being regular open sets, where ∁U = int(X∖U).

This page lists the formal properties:
(vii) Σ^0_F has a least element and a greatest element F, and they are complements of each other. The least element is the 'evident' support {∅_F}, written ∅_Σ, not the empty set. The marginal note explains why: ∅_F is || to everything, so it lies in every polar.
(viii) Σ^0_F is a complete lattice. Inf_i A_i = ∩A_i, since intersections of polars are polars. Sup_i A_i = closure of ∪A_i, which in the topological model is int cl(∪A_i). Both are interchanged by ∁ (De Morgan).
(ix) A ∩ ∁A = ∅_Σ, because the only self-apart figure is ∅_F.
(x) Corollary: A ⊂ B ⇒ A ∩ ∁B = ∅_Σ.
NB: the converse implication is not clear (he suspects it is false). Nor is it clear that finite sups behave like unions. He gives the intuitive reason: a figure contained in the 'sum' of given supports need not lie in any one of them, or be made of pieces lying in them.

In short, Σ^0_F is a complete ortholattice (Birkhoff polarity of an orthogonality space). The next page asks whether it is distributive, i.e. Boolean, and transfers the construction to structures (M, ≤, ≪, ||). The goal is a point-free, 'tame' foundation of analysis situs in which supports or regions are recovered from the single apartness relation between figures.
errors: (vii) as first written calls the least element ∅ (the empty part). It is actually {∅_F} (=∅_Σ), as the asterisked marginal note and the next page ('this time the least element of Σ^0_M is indeed the empty part') correct.

No real error. His doubt in the NB is justified: in an ortholattice, 'A ∧ B^⊥ = 0 ⇒ A ≤ B' holds for all A, B only if the lattice is Boolean (a known characterization). So the converse of (x) is equivalent in strength to the distributivity question he raises on p.64, and it fails in general (e.g. lattices of closed subspaces of Hilbert space).

ideas.what: Closure Ā = cosupp cosupp A induced by a symmetric 'apartness' relation; closed sets = 'supports'
ideas.modern_name: Galois polarity of a symmetric relation / orthogonality space (biorthogonal closure)

ideas.what: Σ^0_F is a complete lattice with inf = ∩, sup = closure of ∪, and involutive antitone complement satisfying A ∧ ∁A = 0
ideas.modern_name: complete ortholattice of biorthogonally closed sets

ideas.what: Topological intuition: the complement of a support is the interior of the complementary region, and sup = int cl(∪); i.e. reconstructing regular-open-type regions from a disjointness relation between figures
ideas.modern_name: regular open algebra / mereotopology (contact and proximity algebras, region-based topology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tarski (geometry of solids, 1929), de Laguna, Whitehead; later Düntsch–Vakarelov, Clarke
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses tame topology but not this formalism

ideas.what: Question whether A ∩ ∁B = 0 ⇒ A ⊂ B, and whether supports are distributive (p.64)
ideas.modern_name: orthomodularity / Booleanness of an ortholattice (quantum-logic-type failure of distributivity)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 'analysis situs' builds a point-free theory of supports from a single apartness relation || between figures. This is exactly the program of mereotopology / region-based topology (Tarski, Whitehead, contact algebras). It is also the orthogonality-space construction of quantum logic, including the same distributivity worry. I know of no literature linking Grothendieck's tame-topology project to mereotopology or orthogonality spaces.
missed.quote: l'intérieur du support complémentaire du support donné A ... Sup A_i = \overline{∪ A_i} ... Il n'est pas clair que l'implication ⟸ soit vraie
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This could inform axiomatizations of 'tame' or o-minimal-style topology in point-free terms. It would also let historians place Grothendieck's late foundations alongside contact-algebra and locale-theoretic approaches.

missed.claim: He leaves open under which conditions on (F, ||) (or on (M, ≤, ≪, ||)) the support lattice Σ^0 is Boolean or distributive. He believes it holds 'in the situations I have in mind'. The precise condition is that A ∧ ∁B = 0 implies A ≤ B, a known equivalent of Booleanness. Identifying geometric axioms on figures that force it was not completed on this page.
missed.quote: Il n'est pas clair ... que les sup finis ... (cela exprime le fait intuitif qu'une 'figure' ... n'est pas forcément ...)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Modest: it is a natural question in region-based topology, already answered in that literature, e.g. by separation-type axioms that make the regions a regular-open (Boolean) algebra.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is standard polarity/ortholattice theory, correctly handled. The only point of interest is that Grothendieck independently rediscovers the mereotopology/orthogonality-space framework as the foundation of his tame analysis situs. He also correctly senses the Boolean-versus-orthomodular issue.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: likely '— l'intérieur du support complémentaire du support donné A' (glossing ∁A); the transcription is broadly right.
(vii): the gloss after 'plus petit élément' reads roughly '(savoir la partie {∅_F} de F)' with marginal 'évident : ∅_F*', not 'faisceau'.
(viii): the arrow annotation after \overline{∪A_i} probably reads '(i.e. int supp(∪A_i))' or 'supp(∪A_i)', giving the topological meaning of the sup.

NB: likely 'Il n'est pas clair que l'implication ⟸ soit vraie (il me paraît fausse)'. In the closing lines, 'minimum' is probably 'réunion' ('une figure contenue dans la réunion de figures n'est pas forcément ...').
